title: unified-rollouts: probing canary + AB + shadow autorollback enhancements
author: Miguel Ortega
description: This PR extends unified rollouts with targeted probing for canary + A/B + shadow workflows and hardens the autorollback engine to use quorumed probing metrics. Motivation: customers running low-traffic canaries and shadow experiments saw delayed or noisy rollouts when metric samples were sparse or when a single probe spike triggered an aggressive rollback. This change adds (1) a lightweight probing stage that issues controlled synthetic requests to exercise tail behavior for short windows, (2) quorum logic where multiple probe sources must agree before triggering autorollback, (3) configurable probe scheduling per rollout stage, and (4) observability telemetry and e2e tests for the probing paths. The implementation touches the rollout controller, the autorollback engine, and the probing scheduler; it keeps defaults conservative and off by default for existing rollouts. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1209) - [x] Unit tests for quorum logic - [x] Integration e2e for canary+shadow probing - [x] Perf benchmark to validate low latency impact - [x] Documentation and console telemetry updates Rollout behavior summary: when enabled, a "probing" stage runs between canary and full traffic. Probes are short-lived synthetic requests routed through the same request path, aggregated with live metrics for decisioning, and evaluated with a configurable quorum and grace period. Autorollback now requires either (a) quorumed probe failures OR (b) live metric breach sustained for configured window. Backwards compatibility: probing is opt-in per rollout and defaults to disabled; all existing rollout policies remain unchanged unless the new fields are set. Related PRs: ties into ENG-1320 (observability of autorollbacks) and earlier autorollback work (see linked PRs in monorepo).
